verification_basis: official public internet sources; source-authority confidence only, not parcel numeric confidence

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 10m
verified_facts: The official 10m DTM covers about 99% of England and is explicitly resampled from the 2m composite using bilinear interpolation.
The 2022 composite spans surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022, uses OS National Grid, metres above Newlyn and OSTN15, and individual source surveys state plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
semantic_limits: The 10m product is a derived coarse secondary product and must never replace the 1m primary parcel source.
Its stated survey RMSE is not a parcel-specific confidence interval.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 Documentation
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 is an open bare-earth height dataset for Great Britain, published as 50m grid points and 10m contours from the same source data.
The documentation states the product is updated annually in July and supplied in 10km tiles.
semantic_limits: Terrain 50 remains a coarse secondary cross-check and not a parcel-scale primary source.
Grid and contour forms are correlated products, not independent observations.

candidates.name: Land and Terrain Portfolio
verified_facts: The OS Land and Terrain Portfolio groups products used to model elevation, slope and ground-surface characteristics.
The portfolio provides the authoritative routing context for Terrain 5 and Terrain 50 documentation.
semantic_limits: Portfolio routing is product-discovery evidence only and contains no parcel-specific height observation.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 - The National Grid
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is supplied across Great Britain in 5km by 5km tiles identified by the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
The OS grid hierarchy uses 100km squares and progressively more specific references for smaller tiles.
semantic_limits: Tile naming and indexing are packaging/location semantics, not vertical accuracy or parcel observation evidence.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 data structure
verified_facts: Terrain 50 grid heights are calculated at pixel centres and tile edges do not share common values.
Mean high and low water use tile-average tide-table heights and can produce small discrete steps between adjacent tiles.
Automatically selected spot heights come from an interpolated surface and are not guaranteed to be true summits.
semantic_limits: Pixel-centre, tidal and spot-height conventions are model semantics, not direct parcel observations.
Tile-edge steps must not be mistaken for real terrain discontinuities without cross-checking.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 pre-requisites
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is supplied as inert data and includes no data-manipulation software.
GML may require translation for a target GIS application, while many GIS packages can read contour GML directly.
semantic_limits: Software translation must preserve numeric height values, CRS and vertical-reference semantics.
Rendering or translation behaviour is not an independent measurement source.
